annotations.title: Thamar.
annotations.text: Chriſt abhorred not to take fleſh of ſome that were il, as he choſe Iudas among his Apoſtles: Let not vs diſdaine to receaue our ſpiritual birth and ſuſtenance of ſuch as be not alwayes good.

annotations.title: Ioſeph.
annotations.text: Ioſeph marying our Lady as neere of kinne (for ſo was the <mn>◦</mn> law) by his pedegree ſheweth hers, and conſequently Chriſts pedegree from Dauid.

annotations.title: Huſband.
annotations.text: True and perfect mariage, and continual liuing in the ſame, without carnal copulation. Aug. lib. 2. Conſen. Euang. c. 1.

annotations.title: Borne in her.
annotations.text: The triple good or perfection of mariage accompliſhed in the parents of Chriſt, to wit, Iſſue, Fidelitie, Sacrament. Aug. de nup. & conc. li. 1. c. 11.

annotations.title: A Virgin.
annotations.text: ◦ Our Sauiour borne in mariage, but yet of a Virgin, would honour both ſtates: and withal, teacheth vs agaynſt Iouinian the old Heretike and theſe of our time, that virginity and the continent life are preferred before mariage that hath carnal copulation. See S. Hierom. adu. Iouin. and S. Greg. Nazianz. Ser. 20. de ſtudio in pauperes, in initio.

annotations.title: A Virgin.
annotations.text: As our Ladie both a virgin and a mother, brought forth Chriſt the head corporally: ſo the Churche a virgin and a mother, bringeth forth the members of this head ſpiritually. Aug. li. de virg. ca. 2.

annotations.title: And bring forth.
annotations.text: ◦ The Heretike Iouinian is here refuted, holding that her virginity was corrupted in bringing forth Chriſt. Aug. hær. 28. Li. 1 cont. Iulian. c. 2.

annotations.title: Til, Firſt-borne.
annotations.text: ◦ Heluidius of old abuſed theſe wordes, til, and, firſt-borne, agaynſt the perpetual virginity of our B. Ladie. Hiero. cont. Helu. Which truth though not expreſſed in Scripture, yet our Aduerſaries alſo do graunt, and Heluidius for denial therof was condemned for an heretike by tradition only. Aug. hær. 84.
